key_insight: Adding an ADR physical PV efficiency model to TSMixer provides limited practical benefit for day-ahead solar power forecasting compared with the purely data-driven baseline.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale PV forecasting, added physics-model complexity may not yield consistent accuracy, geographic transferability, or data-efficiency gains.
method: Combine the ADR physical PV efficiency model with TSMixer.
Integrate physics through feature augmentation and residual learning.
Compare convergence, accuracy, geographic transferability, and limited-data performance.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries; slightly faster training convergence did not translate into consistent test-set improvements.
watch_item: The findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids for day-ahead PV forecasting and should not be generalized to all physics-informed models or forecasting settings.
paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
